front_blocks.md: Define **organisational structure**.

back_blocks.md: An **organisational structure** outlines the **reporting relationships, roles and responsibilities** of employees.

cards.front_md: Define **organisational structure**.
cards.back_md: An **organisational structure** outlines the **reporting relationships, roles and responsibilities** of employees.

front_blocks.md: Define **hierarchy**.

back_blocks.md: A **hierarchy** refers to the **levels of authority** within an organisation, ranked from top to bottom.

cards.front_md: Define **hierarchy**.
cards.back_md: A **hierarchy** refers to the **levels of authority** within an organisation, ranked from top to bottom.

front_blocks.md: Define **chain of command**.

back_blocks.md: The **chain of command** is the **formal line of authority** flowing downward from top management to lower-level employees.

cards.front_md: Define **chain of command**.
cards.back_md: The **chain of command** is the **formal line of authority** flowing downward from top management to lower-level employees.

front_blocks.md: Define **span of control**.

back_blocks.md: **Span of control** is the number of employees a **manager or supervisor directly manages**.

cards.front_md: Define **span of control**.
cards.back_md: **Span of control** is the number of employees a **manager or supervisor directly manages**.

front_blocks.md: A narrow span of control means there are <u>  </u> layers of management.

back_blocks.md: A narrow span of control means there are **more** layers of management.

cards.front_md: A narrow span of control means there are <u>  </u> layers of management.
cards.back_md: A narrow span of control means there are **more** layers of management.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a hierarchical and a flat structure?

back_blocks.md: A **hierarchical** structure has **many levels**, a **long** chain of command and **narrow** span; a **flat** structure has **few levels**, a **short** chain and **wide** span.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a hierarchical and a flat structure?
cards.back_md: A **hierarchical** structure has **many levels**, a **long** chain of command and **narrow** span; a **flat** structure has **few levels**, a **short** chain and **wide** span.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of a hierarchical structure.

back_blocks.md: A **clear structure** of authority, defined **roles**, and it **promotes specialisation**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of a hierarchical structure.
cards.back_md: A **clear structure** of authority, defined **roles**, and it **promotes specialisation**.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of a flat structure.

back_blocks.md: **Faster decision-making**, and a culture of **collaboration** and open communication.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of a flat structure.
cards.back_md: **Faster decision-making**, and a culture of **collaboration** and open communication.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A flat structure usually has a long chain of command.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **flat** structure has a **short** chain of command and **wide** span; a **hierarchical** structure has a **long** chain.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A flat structure usually has a long chain of command.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A **flat** structure has a **short** chain of command and **wide** span; a **hierarchical** structure has a **long** chain.

front_blocks.md: Define **delayering**.

back_blocks.md: **Delayering** is **removing layers** from a hierarchy, which **shortens the chain of command**.

cards.front_md: Define **delayering**.
cards.back_md: **Delayering** is **removing layers** from a hierarchy, which **shortens the chain of command**.

front_blocks.md: Define a **centralised structure**.

back_blocks.md: A **centralised structure** is where authority for decision-making rests with **senior management at the centre**.

cards.front_md: Define a **centralised structure**.
cards.back_md: A **centralised structure** is where authority for decision-making rests with **senior management at the centre**.

front_blocks.md: Define a **decentralised structure**.

back_blocks.md: A **decentralised structure** is where decision-making authority is **delegated further down** the hierarchy.

cards.front_md: Define a **decentralised structure**.
cards.back_md: A **decentralised structure** is where decision-making authority is **delegated further down** the hierarchy.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of a centralised structure.

back_blocks.md: Effective **co-ordination and control**, **fast decision-making**, and **consistency** across the organisation.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of a centralised structure.
cards.back_md: Effective **co-ordination and control**, **fast decision-making**, and **consistency** across the organisation.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of a decentralised structure.

back_blocks.md: Better response to **local conditions**, more **fulfilled and loyal** staff, and it prepares junior managers for **career development**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of a decentralised structure.
cards.back_md: Better response to **local conditions**, more **fulfilled and loyal** staff, and it prepares junior managers for **career development**.

front_blocks.md: A well-designed organisational structure can be shown visually using an organisation <u>  </u>.

back_blocks.md: A well-designed organisational structure can be shown visually using an organisation **chart**.

cards.front_md: A well-designed organisational structure can be shown visually using an organisation <u>  </u>.
cards.back_md: A well-designed organisational structure can be shown visually using an organisation **chart**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A centralised structure ignores the insights of lower-level staff who are closest to customers.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A **disadvantage** of **centralisation** is that it **ignores insights** of lower-level staff who are closer to customers.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A centralised structure ignores the insights of lower-level staff who are closest to customers.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A **disadvantage** of **centralisation** is that it **ignores insights** of lower-level staff who are closer to customers.

front_blocks.md: What does a board of directors do?

back_blocks.md: Makes **key strategic decisions** — e.g. new **corporate policies**, **investment**, and **growth objectives**.

cards.front_md: What does a board of directors do?
cards.back_md: Makes **key strategic decisions** — e.g. new **corporate policies**, **investment**, and **growth objectives**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of a senior manager?

back_blocks.md: To **plan to achieve the business's overall goals**, set **long-term plans and targets**, and contribute to **strategic decisions**.

cards.front_md: What is the role of a senior manager?
cards.back_md: To **plan to achieve the business's overall goals**, set **long-term plans and targets**, and contribute to **strategic decisions**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of a functional manager?

back_blocks.md: To **run a function** (e.g. marketing or finance), **achieve targets** set by directors, and make **operational decisions**.

cards.front_md: What is the role of a functional manager?
cards.back_md: To **run a function** (e.g. marketing or finance), **achieve targets** set by directors, and make **operational decisions**.

front_blocks.md: What does a supervisor or team leader do?

back_blocks.md: **Report problems**, **pass on instructions**, and take **simple decisions** such as allocating jobs.

cards.front_md: What does a supervisor or team leader do?
cards.back_md: **Report problems**, **pass on instructions**, and take **simple decisions** such as allocating jobs.

front_blocks.md: In a department store, sales assistants and customer service reps are examples of <u>  </u> staff.

back_blocks.md: In a department store, sales assistants and customer service reps are examples of **operational** staff.

cards.front_md: In a department store, sales assistants and customer service reps are examples of <u>  </u> staff.
cards.back_md: In a department store, sales assistants and customer service reps are examples of **operational** staff.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between operational and support staff?

back_blocks.md: **Operational** staff do the **core tasks** directed by managers; **support** staff assist with **non-core** operations (e.g. cleaners, IT technicians).

cards.front_md: What is the difference between operational and support staff?
cards.back_md: **Operational** staff do the **core tasks** directed by managers; **support** staff assist with **non-core** operations (e.g. cleaners, IT technicians).

front_blocks.md: Define **delegation**.

back_blocks.md: **Delegation** is giving **responsibility for specific tasks** to subordinates, usually **transferring authority** from manager to subordinate.

cards.front_md: Define **delegation**.
cards.back_md: **Delegation** is giving **responsibility for specific tasks** to subordinates, usually **transferring authority** from manager to subordinate.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of delegation for managers.

back_blocks.md: It lets managers **concentrate on important tasks**, **measure staff performance**, and can **reduce errors**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of delegation for managers.
cards.back_md: It lets managers **concentrate on important tasks**, **measure staff performance**, and can **reduce errors**.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of delegation for workers.

back_blocks.md: Workers feel **empowered and motivated**, gain **training**, and find work more **interesting and rewarding**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of delegation for workers.
cards.back_md: Workers feel **empowered and motivated**, gain **training**, and find work more **interesting and rewarding**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Delegation is particularly important in a flat organisational structure.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Delegation** is especially important in a **flat** structure, where managers have **wide spans of control**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Delegation is particularly important in a flat organisational structure.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

**Delegation** is especially important in a **flat** structure, where managers have **wide spans of control**.

back_blocks.md: Some managers are reluctant to delegate because they lose some **control** over decision-making.

All managers are always happy to delegate authority to their subordinates.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Some managers are **reluctant to delegate** — e.g. **autocratic** leaders, or those who feel **threatened** by skilled subordinates.

front_blocks.md: Define a **functional area**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional area** is a **group of workers with similar skills** who carry out a specific organisational role.

cards.front_md: Define a **functional area**.
cards.back_md: A **functional area** is a **group of workers with similar skills** who carry out a specific organisational role.

front_blocks.md: Name the four main functional areas of a business.

back_blocks.md: **Human Resources**, **Finance**, **Marketing**, and **Production**.

cards.front_md: Name the four main functional areas of a business.
cards.back_md: **Human Resources**, **Finance**, **Marketing**, and **Production**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the Human Resources function?

back_blocks.md: **Managing the workforce** — recruitment, training, **industrial relations**, and **health and safety** compliance.

cards.front_md: What is the role of the Human Resources function?
cards.back_md: **Managing the workforce** — recruitment, training, **industrial relations**, and **health and safety** compliance.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the Finance function?

back_blocks.md: **Managing the organisation's money** — recording transactions, paying **bills and salaries**, setting **budgets**, and preparing the **annual report**.

cards.front_md: What is the role of the Finance function?
cards.back_md: **Managing the organisation's money** — recording transactions, paying **bills and salaries**, setting **budgets**, and preparing the **annual report**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the Marketing function?

back_blocks.md: **Understanding customer needs** — market **research**, **distribution**, **pricing**, and persuading customers to buy.

cards.front_md: What is the role of the Marketing function?
cards.back_md: **Understanding customer needs** — market **research**, **distribution**, **pricing**, and persuading customers to buy.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the Production function?

back_blocks.md: **Creating the product or service** — ensuring **quality**, sourcing **raw materials**, **designing and testing** products, and **stock management**.

cards.front_md: What is the role of the Production function?
cards.back_md: **Creating the product or service** — ensuring **quality**, sourcing **raw materials**, **designing and testing** products, and **stock management**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Functional areas work independently and never need to cooperate.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Functional areas must work together** — e.g. Finance sets the budget that Marketing spends on promotion.

front_blocks.md: Why might a business outsource a functional area?

back_blocks.md: To **reduce costs** and access **specialist advice** from providers who would be expensive to employ directly.
